parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘systematic desensitisation’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the cognitive explanation of phobias.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain two strengths of the cognitive explanation of phobias.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the treatment and management of obsessive-compulsive and related disorders.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate the treatment and management of obsessive-compulsive and related disorders,
including a discussion about determinism versus free-will. 
Psychology and consumer behaviour

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘effective slogans’ in advertising.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the study by Fischer et al. (1991) on brand recognition in advertising.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Discuss the use of children as participants in the study by Fischer et al.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about intuitive thinking and its imperfections in
consumer decision-making (thinking fast and thinking slow, choice blindness, advertising and
false memory).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about intuitive thinking and its imperfections in
consumer decision-making (thinking fast and thinking slow, choice blindness, advertising and
false memory), including a discussion of practical applications. 
Psychology and health

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘psychogenic pain’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe cognitive redefinition as a technique for managing pain.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain one similarity and one difference between cognitive redefinition and biochemical
techniques for managing pain.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about measuring non-adherence to medical
advice.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about measuring non-adherence to medical
advice, including a discussion about self-reports. 
Psychology and organisations

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
McClelland proposed the theory of achievement motivation which included three types of
needs.
Identify two of these needs, other than the need for achievement.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how equity theory (Adams, 1963) explains motivation at work.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one weakness of equity theory.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about leaders and followers in organisations
(leader-member exchange model/individualised leadership model, followership, measuring
leadership).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about leaders and followers in organisations
(leader-member exchange model/individualised leadership model, followership, measuring
leadership), including a discussion on reductionism versus holism.
